thread:
Maria: Noticing a sudden throughput drop and multiple worker restarts in us-west-2 dedicated pool around 2026-03-18T03:45Z. Pasting a short log snippet and initial readout.

sre-bot: Incident created: INC-20260318-uw2-churn (priority: high) — paging oncall

Maria: log snippet:
```
[03:45:07] worker-11 ERROR: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory
[03:45:08] worker-11 INFO: restarting worker pid=7441
[03:45:12] runtime WARN: kernel-selector: fallback to safe_gemm for head=4
[03:45:15] worker-05 WARN: allocator: fragmented free extents=2
```

Dave: Pulled perf traces from three hosts. Kernel selector flip at ~03:45:05 — selector bumped to fallback after a quantile threshold tweak. The fallback uses a different GEMM ordering and allocates larger temporaries; trace shows a burst of ephemeral allocations and high peak resident.

Jia: KV shard picture looks bad during the window. We had a canary active that extended prefix retention on dedicated (rolled last night). `kv_shards_per_request` median jumped ~3.1x between 03:40-03:50. Heatmap: 
```
03:30-03:40 small tight distribution
03:40-03:50 wide tail, more large shards
03:50-04:00 still elevated but tapering
```

Leo: The adaptive-batching/kv-linger canary was intended to reduce cold misses for long dialogs, but that raises per-worker resident memory. Combined with the fallback kernel's temp buffers, the allocator can't compact free space fast enough.

Dave: Two interacting failure modes: 1) increased working set from longer-lived KV entries, 2) fallback kernel uses 1.6-2x larger scratch buffers. The gpu allocator's free lists fragment; after a few cycles some cudaMallocs fail leading to worker restarts. Traces attached in the perf bucket.

Maria: Immediate mitigation suggestions?

Lee (oncall): Rolling back the kv-linger canary on dedicated and reverting the kernel-selector override on the affected pool. Also bumping allocator trim frequency and setting a temporary per-request kv shard cap. Doing changes now.

ops-bot: rollback started: deploy_id=canary-20260317-kvlinger-roll by Lee

Dave: Commands executed:
```
infractl deploy rollback --pool=us-west-2-dedicated --tag=canary-20260317-kvlinger
infractl config set us-west-2 allocator.trim_interval_sec=10
infractl config set serving.kv.max_shards_per_request=4
```

ops-bot: rollback finished: deploy_id=canary-20260317-kvlinger-roll status=success

Jia: Post-rollback metrics: kv_shards median down ~3x, cache miss and tail latencies returning to baseline. Fragmentation alerts decreased. A few older hosts still show transient restarts likely due to leftover fragmentation; those recovered after scheduled restarts.

Dave: Short-term hotfix: enabled `ALLOCATOR_FORCE_COALESCE=true` on the pool to trigger a compaction shim between large allocations. Also added a soft-guard that rejects overly-large temp allocations in fallback path to avoid cascading OOM.

Maria: Nice. What are the long-term follow-ups to avoid recurrence?

Leo: Action items:
- Pause adaptive prefix-linger on dedicated until we add simulator tests (owner: Leo)
- Add a kernel-selector memory probe that measures transient temp allocation footprint before flipping production (owner: Dave)
- Implement allocator compaction hook for long-running workers + tighten default trim interval (owner: eng-runtime)
- CI perf test combining extended-prefix retention + quantized kernels to catch mem blowups (owner: eng-ml)

Dave: Uploading artifact bundle and a short analysis (flamegraphs, allocation traces, kernel footprints): https://internal.redwood/prof/1779001111/kernel-kv-churn

Maria: Thanks all :thumbsup: Leaving this incident open for 24h monitoring and tracking action items. Will mark mitigated after 2 hours with no restarts.

sre-bot: Incident INC-20260318-uw2-churn status=mitigated — monitoring
